queue_items.claim: The book-wide saints-term digit (26 verses) counts a consonantal substring, not the two spellings the sentence names; the named object occurs in 10 verses, and the 26 includes a different lexeme.
queue_items.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative, observed_substrate_signals[3] and device_notes all read: the saints-term (chasidim/chasidav) recurring at 149:1, 149:5, and 149:9 (3 of 3 Psalm 149 members; 26 verses book-wide, skeleton tier). Re-swept at skeleton tier over the MT verse map: the contiguous consonantal substring chet-samekh-yod-dalet occurs in exactly 26 verses -- that is where the digit comes from -- but the two spellings the sentence NAMES, חֲסִידִ֣ים (oshb:Ps.149.5) and חֲסִידָ֗יו (oshb:Ps.149.9), occur in only 10 verses book-wide (2 and 8 respectively). The 16-verse remainder is other forms (MT 4:4, 12:2, 16:10, 18:26, 32:6, 43:1, 50:5, 52:11, 79:2, 86:2, 89:20, 104:17, 132:9, 132:16, 145:10, 145:17), and MT 104:17's member is חֲ֝סִידָ֗ה -- the stork, a different lexeme -- exactly the contained-substring trap the book's sweep hazard catalog names. The load-bearing half of the sentence, 3 of 3 Psalm 149 members, is byte-TRUE and is what keeps the whole_psalm rival live at medium confidence, so the defective digit is not alone load-bearing. The same sentence is carried on the paired row for 149:5-9 (there as 2 of 3 members; 26 verses book-wide), so any cure is a seam-pair cure installed on both.
queue_items.proposed_change: Either rename the object to match the digit (the saints-root chet-samekh-yod-dalet as a consonantal substring: 26 verses book-wide, skeleton tier, including the homographic stork at MT 104:17) or keep the named spellings and correct the digit to 10 verses book-wide; install the same wording on the paired 149:5-9 row.

trigger_dispositions.grounds: Three occurrences of psalm_device_inventory.json in row prose: boundary_rationale (opener device, psalm_device_inventory.json verse-initial list), observed_substrate_signals[0], and device_notes (opens at web:Ps.149.1 and closes at web:Ps.149.9 (psalm_device_inventory.json)). REG TEST 2 re-derivation from bytes: the frame claim is TRUE -- הַ֥לְלוּ יָ֨הּ opens MT 149:1 and the same pair closes MT 149:9, and Ps 149 is an identity psalm, so the web: refs are in the right space; the three-of-three saints-term recurrence is TRUE (חֲסִידִֽים oshb:Ps.149.1, חֲסִידִ֣ים oshb:Ps.149.5, חֲסִידָ֗יו oshb:Ps.149.9); the assembly imagery is confined to 149:1-3 and the sword-noun first appears at MT 149:6; and prefix-conjugation forms do stand in every verse from MT 149:2 through MT 149:5, which is why the row honestly calls the seam a discourse turn in setting, not a formal disjunctive marker, and holds at medium with the whole_psalm rival live (Ps 149 has 9 verses, just past the book's short-psalm whole_psalm range, so the rival is correctly weighed rather than dismissed). The one companion digit that does NOT survive is the book-wide saints-term count (separate medium finding below). Register defect at low severity.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Psalm 149 opens under the hallelu-Yah frame (opener device, psalm_device_inventory.json verse-initial list) — הַ֥לְלוּ יָ֨הּ (oshb:Ps.149.1) — with “Praise Yahweh! Sing to Yahweh a new song, his praise in the assembly of the saints” (web:Ps.149.1), the assembly named בִּקְהַ֥ל חֲסִידִֽים (oshb:Ps.149.1). The unit runs through the causal grounding clause כִּֽי רוֹצֶ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה (oshb:Ps.149.4), “For Yahweh takes pleasure in his people. He crowns the humble with salvation” (web:Ps.149.4), which closes the reason for praise. At web:Ps.149.5 the same prefix-conjugation mood continues on a changed setting — the saints on their beds rather than the dancing assembly of web:Ps.149.3 — and carries the sword theme of web:Ps.149.6, unheralded in 149:1-4; the seam is a discourse turn in setting, not a formal disjunctive marker, since the mood itself runs unbroken from web:Ps.149.2 through web:Ps.149.5.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating Ps 149 as one undivided whole_psalm row is set aside here: 149:5's shift from public dance-assembly to private posture and the unheralded sword of 149:6 mark a real discourse turn, though the saints-term (chasidim/chasidav) recurring at 149:1, 149:5, and 149:9 (3 of 3 Psalm 149 members; 26 verses book-wide, skeleton tier) keeps the alternative live enough that confidence stays medium rather than high.
observed_substrate_signals: assembly imagery (dance, tambourine, harp) confined to 149:1-3 (web:Ps.149.1, web:Ps.149.3)
the causal 'for' clause at oshb:Ps.149.4 closes the summons before the setting changes
the saints-term (chasidim/chasidav) recurs at 149:1, 149:5, and 149:9 (3 of 3 Psalm 149 members; 26 verses book-wide, skeleton tier), bridging the proposed seam
shipped_row.device_notes: The parent relation points every row to Psalm 149. Its hallelu-Yah frame opens at web:Ps.149.1 and closes at web:Ps.149.9 (psalm_device_inventory.json), bracketing both of the psalm's proposed strophes; the saints-term (chasidim) recurs at 149:1, 149:5, and 149:9 (3 of 3 Psalm 149 members; 26 verses book-wide, skeleton tier) as the assembly's own self-designation across the seam.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: הַֽלְל֣וּ אֶת יְ֭הוָה מִן הָאָ֑רֶץ (oshb:Ps.148.7) opens the second panel, “Praise Yahweh from the earth, you great sea creatures, and all depths,” (web:Ps.148.7), through weather (web:Ps.148.8), mountains and trees (web:Ps.148.9), animals and birds (web:Ps.148.10), and human classes from kings to children (web:Ps.148.11-web:Ps.148.12); the same purpose-clause formula that closed the heavens panel recurs almost word for word, יְהַלְל֤וּ אֶת שֵׁ֬ם יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Ps.148.13), “Let them praise Yahweh's name, for his name alone is exalted.” (web:Ps.148.13) — echoing web:Ps.148.5's own יְֽ֭הַֽלְלוּ אֶת שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ps.148.5) — and the psalm closes on Israel's own horn lifted up and the frame's own closing formula, הַֽלְלוּ יָֽהּ (oshb:Ps.148.14), “Praise Yah!” (web:Ps.148.14) answering the opening frame at web:Ps.148.1.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Subdividing the earth roster's own long catalog (web:Ps.148.7-12) from its closing couplet (web:Ps.148.13-14) into two rows was considered, but the purpose-clause echo of web:Ps.148.5 ties the whole panel's own catalog to its own close as one sustained unit, mirroring the heavens panel's own shape.
observed_substrate_signals: MT 148:7's own min ha'aretz ('from the earth') answers min hashamayim ('from the heavens') at MT 148:1, the roster's own two-panel turn
the purpose-clause wording at web:Ps.148.13 (yehalelu et shem YHWH) echoes web:Ps.148.5's own wording (ye-halelu et shem YHWH) almost token for token, byte-checked
the closing hallelu-Yah at web:Ps.148.14 is verse-final, matching the opening verse-initial occurrence at web:Ps.148.1

next_row.boundary_rationale: At web:Ps.149.5, יַעְלְז֣וּ חֲסִידִ֣ים (oshb:Ps.149.5) continues the same yod-preformative prefix-conjugation mood already running since web:Ps.149.2, now on a changed setting — “Let the saints rejoice in honor. Let them sing for joy on their beds” (web:Ps.149.5) — and the content shifts from the assembly's praise-calls of 149:1-4 into the equipment of judgment: “May the high praises of God be in their mouths, and a two-edged sword in their hand” (web:Ps.149.6), the sword itself named וְחֶ֖רֶב פִּֽיפִיּ֣וֹת בְּיָדָֽם (oshb:Ps.149.6). 149:7-9 continue in infinitive-construct purpose clauses (“to execute vengeance”, web:Ps.149.7; “to bind their kings”, web:Ps.149.8) rather than the jussive mood of 149:2-5, closing at the hallelu-Yah frame's second bookend, הַֽלְלוּ יָֽהּ (oshb:Ps.149.9), “Praise Yah!” (web:Ps.149.9).
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 149:5-9 back into one undivided unit with 149:1-4 is set aside for the same reason the seam is drawn at 149:4|5: the setting shift at 149:5 and the unheralded sword of 149:6 are not anticipated in the assembly's dance-and-instrument praise of 149:1-3, though the saints-term's echo at 149:5 and 149:9 (2 of 3 Psalm 149 members; 26 verses book-wide, skeleton tier) keeps the alternative from being dismissed outright.
observed_substrate_signals: the prefix-conjugation pair at 149:5, continuing the same mood active since 149:2, sets a private posture ('on their beds') distinct from 149:1-3's public assembly
וְחֶ֖רֶב פִּֽיפִיּ֣וֹת בְּיָדָֽם (oshb:Ps.149.6) introduces the sword with no antecedent in 149:1-4 (the sword-noun's 3-consonant stem: 1 verse in Psalm 149, skeleton tier; 24 verses book-wide)

next_row.device_notes: לְכָל חֲסִידָ֗יו (oshb:Ps.149.9) closes the saints-designation opened at 149:1 and repeated at 149:5, and the psalm's hallelu-Yah frame shuts here after opening at web:Ps.149.1.
